name: GLP-1 and obesity
thesis: Obesity drugs are moving from a supply constrained, high price injectable market to a mass market of cheaper pills and government covered access, so volume is exploding while price per patient falls. Lilly has pulled ahead of Novo on efficacy, supply and the oral launch, and its tirzepatide franchise is now the largest drug franchise in the world by quarterly sales. The 2026 policy turn (TrumpRx pricing, $50 Medicare copay via the GLP-1 Bridge starting July 2026, and the $274 negotiated Medicare semaglutide price in 2027) trades margin for volume. Picks and shovels shift as the mix moves to pills: peptide and small molecule API capacity, CDMOs and devices still grow, but the next leg of volume growth favors API and tablet capacity over pens. Second order effects on food, medtech, diagnostics and insurers are real but slower than headlines suggest.

facts: Q2 2026 revenue rose 48% to $23.0 billion, with volume up 60% and realized prices down 13% (Lilly Q2 2026, August 2026).
Q2 2026 Mounjaro revenue rose 91% to $9.9 billion and Zepbound rose 46% to $4.9 billion.
Lilly raised 2026 revenue guidance to $85.0 billion to $87.0 billion and non GAAP EPS to $35.50 to $36.50.
FDA approved orforglipron (Foundayo) for weight loss on April 1, 2026; launched April 6, 2026 at $149/month self pay for the starting dose and $50 Medicare Part D price from July 2026.
Retatrutide TRIUMPH-1 showed 28.3% weight loss at 80 weeks; Lilly plans to file in Q1 2027.

pipeline.timing: Filed December 2025; decision expected around year end 2026
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Approval gives Novo a next gen injectable to defend share; adds demand for amylin analog peptide API and pens. A miss or weak label shifts more share to Lilly.
Triple agonist with about 28% to 30% weight loss raises the efficacy bar; drives more injectable peptide API and autoinjector demand at Lilly.

Medicare beneficiaries pay $50 per month; CMS runs prior authorization centrally. Large volume add for LLY and NVO at lower net prices. BALANCE model will not run in Part D in 2027 but runs in Medicaid from May 2026 to 2031.
$274 per month (higher dose Wegovy $385) versus $959 list; reduces Novo US net price and sets a reference price for the class.

pipeline.timing: Dosing began February 2026; completion around late 2029
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Long dated; keeps Novo relevant in next gen but no revenue before about 2030.

pipeline.product: Oral VK2735 phase 3 (Viking) and MariTide phase 3 (Amgen)
pipeline.timing: Viking oral phase 3 start planned Q3 2026; Amgen MARITIME program ongoing
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Competitors add CDMO demand (Viking outsources manufacturing); M&A optionality for Viking.

pipeline.product: Lilly US API mega sites (Virginia $5 billion, Houston $6.5 billion, Huntsville $6 billion)
pipeline.what_changes_for_suppliers: Big demand for process equipment, engineering and construction; over time Lilly insources more API, which limits upside for third party peptide makers.

layers.name: Drug developers and brand owners
layers.why: The two incumbents capture most of the profit pool, with a crowded set of challengers aiming for monthly dosing, amylin combos or orals.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Clinical efficacy and manufacturing scale are moats; Lilly and Novo have both, challengers are years behind.

companies.name: Eli Lilly
companies.note: Leader on efficacy and supply; 2026 revenue guidance $85 to $87 billion.

companies.name: Novo Nordisk
companies.role: Semaglutide (Ozempic, Wegovy, Wegovy pill), CagriSema, amycretin
companies.note: Q2 2026 adjusted sales +7% CER; 2026 outlook raised to 0% to minus 6%. Wegovy pill passed 5 million US prescriptions.

companies.name: Amgen
companies.note: Phase 2 weight loss up to about 20% at one year.

companies.name: Pfizer
companies.role: Acquired Metsera (about $10 billion, closed November 2025): monthly GLP-1 and amylin candidates
companies.note: Late entrant, years from launch.

companies.name: Viking Therapeutics
companies.note: Binary clinical and M&A volatility; rich option premiums.

companies.name: Structure Therapeutics
companies.note: Clinical stage; status of 2026 data unverified.

companies.name: Zealand Pharma
companies.role: Petrelintide amylin analog partnered with Roche
companies.note: Copenhagen listing; limited US access.

companies.name: Roche
companies.role: Obesity pipeline via Zealand partnership and Carmot acquisition
companies.note: US OTC RHHBY.

layers.name: API and peptide manufacturing
layers.why: Pills need far more API per patient than injections, so the shift to orals and the volume surge make API capacity a key constraint.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Peptide synthesis and large scale small molecule capacity take years to build; Lilly is spending tens of billions on US API sites finishing into the 2030s.

companies.name: Lonza
companies.role: Large CDMO for biologics and small molecules
companies.note: US OTC LZAGY. Specific GLP-1 contracts not verified.

companies.name: Bachem
companies.note: Peptide synthesis specialist; customer names not disclosed (GLP-1 exposure widely assumed, unverified).

companies.name: PolyPeptide Group
companies.note: Swiss listing only.

companies.name: Siegfried
companies.note: Potential beneficiary of oral small molecule GLP-1 outsourcing (unverified).

companies.name: Samsung Biologics
companies.note: Korea listing.

companies.name: Thermo Fisher Scientific
companies.role: CDMO (Patheon), bioprocess consumables and lab tools
companies.note: Diversified; GLP-1 is a small share.

companies.name: Danaher
companies.role: Chromatography and filtration used in peptide purification
companies.note: Picks and shovels for manufacturing scale up.

companies.name: Repligen
companies.note: Small cap tools play.

layers.name: Fill finish and CDMO sterile capacity
layers.why: Injectables still dominate revenue, and every pen needs sterile filling in cartridges or syringes.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Novo bought three Catalent fill finish sites for $11 billion; capacity has caught up from the 2023 to 2024 shortage, so this layer is less tight than in 2024.

companies.name: Catalent (Novo Holdings)
companies.role: Fill finish CDMO; three sites sold to Novo Nordisk
companies.note: Taken private by Novo Holdings for $16.5 billion.

companies.name: Stevanato Group
companies.role: Glass cartridges, syringes, vials and fill finish equipment
companies.note: High value cartridges for pens.

companies.name: Gerresheimer
companies.role: Glass and plastic primary packaging, pen components
companies.note: German listing.

companies.name: Schott Pharma
companies.role: Pharma glass cartridges and prefillable syringes
companies.note: German listing.

layers.name: Injection devices: pens, autoinjectors and components
layers.why: Each weekly injection patient uses multiple pens per month; device makers grow with injectable volume.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Device platforms are qualified per drug, so switching is slow; pills may cap long term pen growth.

companies.name: West Pharmaceutical Services
companies.role: Elastomer plungers and seals, containment for GLP-1 pens
companies.note: Components inside most injectables.

companies.name: Becton Dickinson
companies.note: Large diversified medtech.

companies.name: Ypsomed
companies.role: Autoinjectors and pens; supply deal with Novo Nordisk
companies.note: Swiss listing; launched LyoTwist dual chamber device February 2026.

companies.name: SHL Medical
companies.note: Private.

layers.name: Distribution, pharmacy and telehealth
layers.why: Direct to consumer channels (LillyDirect, NovoCare, TrumpRx) and telehealth are taking share from traditional pharmacy for cash pay patients.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Many channels; manufacturers increasingly sell direct.

companies.name: Hims and Hers Health
companies.note: Settled with Novo in 2026: stops compounded semaglutide, offers branded semaglutide at telehealth parity price.

companies.name: CVS Health
companies.note: PBM formulary choices between Lilly and Novo move share.

companies.name: Cigna (Evernorth, Express Scripts)
companies.note: Manages employer GLP-1 spend.

layers.name: Second order beneficiaries: diagnostics, monitoring and nutrition
layers.why: More patients under treatment means more labs, glucose monitoring and protein focused nutrition.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Competitive markets; benefit is volume, not scarcity.

companies.name: Dexcom
companies.note: GLP-1 users with diabetes still use CGMs; feared headwind did not materialize as of 2025 (verify latest).

companies.name: Abbott Laboratories
companies.role: Libre CGMs and adult nutrition (protein shakes)
companies.note: Diversified.

companies.name: Quest Diagnostics
companies.role: Lab testing for metabolic monitoring and prior authorization
companies.note: Benefit is a hypothesis, not a reported revenue line.

companies.name: BellRing Brands
companies.note: Protein intake to preserve muscle on GLP-1 is a frequent recommendation; link to sales unverified.

layers.name: Second order losers: snacks, some medtech, weight loss services
layers.why: Lower appetite cuts calories and snack volumes in GLP-1 households, and drugs substitute for some procedures and devices.
layers.bottleneck_reason: Not a supply layer; listed to frame who is hurt.

companies.name: PepsiCo
companies.note: Reported five straight quarters of declining snack volumes (Food Dive trendline, cause is mixed).

companies.name: Mondelez International
companies.note: North American revenue slipped 4% per Food Dive trendline.

companies.name: Hershey
companies.note: Mixed: Ice Breakers retail sales up over 8% in Q1 2026.

companies.name: ResMed
companies.note: Zepbound approved for obstructive sleep apnea in December 2024; ResMed says GLP-1s bring patients into care, so impact is debated.

companies.name: WW International
companies.role: Weight Watchers, now offers GLP-1 clinic
companies.note: Restructured in 2025 bankruptcy; legacy diet business hurt.

second_order.idea: Volume over price: net price erosion offset by Medicare and cash pay volume
second_order.why: Lilly Q2 2026 showed +60% volume and -13% price. The $274 Medicare semaglutide price in 2027 and $149 pill starting price extend that trade off.

second_order.idea: Pills shift value from devices to API and tablet capacity
second_order.why: Orforglipron and the Wegovy pill need large API volumes; pens grow slower in a pill heavy world.

second_order.idea: Gum, mints, protein and portion controlled foods win share inside food
second_order.why: Confectionery and snack mix shifts toward functional and low calorie items rather than collapsing.
Weight loss may drive wardrobe replacement; no verified company data, treat as speculative.

second_order.idea: Insurers and employers face higher drug spend near term, lower medical spend long term (hypothesis)
second_order.why: Outcome data on cardiovascular and other events could shift payer economics over years; not verified in 2026 results.

risks.risk: Faster than expected price erosion from government deals, Medicare negotiation and competition
risks.signal: Realized price declines in quarterly reports; 2027 IRA selected drug list including tirzepatide (unverified timing).
FDA label changes, FAERS reports, large observational studies.
FDA enforcement actions; telehealth pricing below branded cash prices.

risks.risk: Clinical failure or delay for next gen assets
risks.signal: CagriSema FDA decision around year end 2026; phase 3 readouts.

risks.risk: Insourcing by Lilly and Novo squeezes third party CDMO and API makers
risks.signal: Lilly and Novo capex announcements; CDMO order commentary.

risks.risk: Persistence problem: patients stop drugs and regain weight
risks.signal: Real world adherence data from PBMs and Medicare Bridge.
